hook: Sleeping more is not the solution to feeling tired. Sleeping at the wrong time is often the entire problem.
topic: Sleep timing vs. duration — circadian alignment as the primary variable
body:
**If you've tried increasing your sleep time and still feel unrested, timing is the variable you haven't adjusted yet.**

Your circadian system regulates the structure of sleep across the night. The proportion of slow-wave sleep you get is highest in the early cycles. The proportion of REM is highest in the late cycles. These distributions are not negotiable — they follow the clock, not the bedtime.

When your sleep is misaligned — when you're going to bed two or three hours after your biological clock says night has arrived — you're compressing the early cycles, getting less slow-wave, and the whole architecture shifts. You can sleep nine hours in the wrong window and wake up less restored than someone who slept seven in the right one.

Alignment matters more than duration. Your body needs sleep at the time it's biologically prepared to use it — not at whatever time you get around to lying down.

If you've added hours and it hasn't worked, this is the next variable to look at.

Protocol for resetting alignment is linked in my bio.
